column4: Floodwater sheds foam and molten metal sheds dross; the scum vanishes while what benefits people remains, exactly staging ore, residue, and the source's definition of tahsil as isolating what stays.
The just scales bring forth even a mustard seed's weight and God suffices as reckoner, joining the section's inner grain to its final, exact account.
A mustard seed hidden in rock, heaven, or earth is brought out by God, who is لطيف خبير; hidden grain, extraction, minuteness, and divine expertise meet in one scene.
The exact vessel ما في صدوركم is tested and what is in the hearts is purified with وليمحص, making the section's laborious inner sorting explicit in the aftermath of Uhud.
Whether people disclose or conceal what is within themselves, God calls them to account for it; hidden interior and final reckoning are directly joined.
الحب ذو العصف places grain together with its leafy husk or straw, the concrete kernel-and-cover scene used by the source's dictionary explanation.
God knows even a grain in the earth's darknesses, and every moist or dry thing is in a clear record; a hidden kernel and exhaustive knowledge meet.
God separates الخبيث from الطيب, heaps the bad together, and consigns it to Hell, a direct eschatological sorting and gathering scene.
God does not leave the believers' mixed company as it is until He distinguishes the bad from the good, directly matching tahsil as discriminating what the mixture contains.
وإذا القبور بعثرت repeats both the graves and the very scattering verb of 100:9, supplying the bodily unearthing that precedes the breast's sorting.
يوم تبلى السرائر names the day when concealed inner things are tested, a concise parallel to the exposure and examination of what breasts contain.
People with diseased hearts are asked whether they suppose God will never bring out their grudges; the concealed inner deposit is explicitly extracted.
The commanded warning uses the same ما في صدوركم and says that concealing or disclosing it makes no difference to God's knowledge.
On the day people are presented, لا تخفى منكم خافية: no hidden thing remains hidden, stating the result of the section's inner exposure.
The record omits neither small nor great, and people find all they did present; this is the section's account reduced to its complete final total.
People fold their breasts and cover themselves to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and reveal and knows the very contents of breasts.
God knows the furtive glance and وما تخفي الصدور, distinguishing an almost invisible outward act from what the breast conceals.
Concealed and public speech are set side by side because God knows بذات الصدور, directly linking disclosure, concealment, and the breast's contents.
Following 67:13's concealed speech and breasts, the Creator's knowledge is grounded in الخبير; this ayah supplies the same expert knower who underwrites 100:11.
God knows what people conceal and reveal and is عليم بذات الصدور, placing outer disclosure and the interior vessel in the same assertion.
God effaces falsehood, establishes truth, and knows the contents of breasts; discrimination between what disappears and what is established is tied to inner knowledge.
The deserters say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, while God is خبير بما تعملون; appearance, inner reality, and expert knowledge converge.
Some say belief with their mouths although their hearts have not believed, and the ayah speaks of hearts God has not willed to purify, joining inner truth to refinement.
They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, while God knows best what they conceal; the outer shell and hidden content are explicitly opposed.
Hatred has appeared from mouths, but what breasts hide is greater, making the unseen interior exceed the visible disclosure.
The same people profess belief when they meet believers and bite their fingers in rage when alone; the ayah closes with God's knowledge of breast contents, completing 3:118's hidden hatred.
The hypocrites fear a surah will disclose what is in their hearts, and God promises to bring out the very thing they fear will be exposed.
God knows both what their breasts conceal and what they announce, exactly articulating the source's interior-versus-appearance distinction.
The Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they announce; this knowledge grounds His choosing and judgment in the ayah's context.
Secret affection toward enemies is set against God's knowledge of what is hidden and declared, directly placing concealed love under divine scrutiny.
A confidential statement is disclosed, God informs the Prophet of it, and the exchange ends with العليم الخبير; hidden content is made known by the Expert.
Concealing testimony is called a sin of the heart, and God knows what people do; a suppressed outward truth becomes an inner moral deposit.
What people repeatedly earn forms a rust over their hearts, giving a concrete picture of years of acts accumulating upon the inner core.
The soul is shown both its depravity and its piety, identifying the opposed inner contents on which purification and failure operate.
Success belongs to the one who purifies the soul, a direct inward counterpart to the section's careful separation and refining.
God is فالق الحب والنوى, the cleaver of grain and date stone, so the literal kernel is opened and life is drawn from what enclosed it.
Believers must spend from the good things they earn and from earth's produce rather than deliberately selecting the bad, combining harvest, wealth, and moral sorting.
Giving from desire for God's pleasure and inner firmness is likened to a garden yielding abundantly, supplying the inwardly sound counterpart to 2:264's stripped surface.
The question about what people sow establishes the grain under examination and asks them to look beneath their assumed control of the harvest.
The next question distinguishes human sowing from God's causing growth, separating the visible act from the agency that produces its substance.
God could make the crop shattered debris, leaving cultivators bewildered; the valued grain can end as the useless residue imagined by the threshing scene.
Solomon says إني أحببت حب الخير in the horse scene, an especially close lexical counterpart to 100:8's لحب الخير whose attachment is later sorted.
وتحبون المال حبا جما names an immense love of wealth, the attachment that the section locates as the grain deep within the breast.
People cannot reach righteousness until they spend from what they love, making relinquishment of the beloved thing the test that discloses love's quality.
Hoarded gold and silver embody accumulated loved wealth that is withheld rather than spent, preparing the material that the next ayah exposes by fire.
The hoarded metal is heated and made to brand bodies, turning concealed accumulation into an exposed judgment and joining gold, fire, and account.
Competition for increase distracts people, opening a sequence in which accumulation lasts only until the graves and eventual questioning.
حتى زرتم المقابر abruptly carries worldly accumulation into the graves, paralleling the movement from intense attachment to opened graves in Surah 100.
Each soul must inspect what it has sent ahead for tomorrow, and God is خبير بما تعملون; self-audit and the divine Expert meet.
God's testing distinguishes strivers and the steadfast and tests أخباركم; this other خ ب ر form makes people's true report emerge through examination.
The earth brings out its burdens, a close bodily counterpart to emptied graves before hidden inner deeds are displayed.
The earth tells أخبارها after discharging its burdens, using another خ ب ر form for the report that exposed creation itself gives.
People depart in separate groups so that their deeds may be shown to them, setting the sorting and display completed by 99:7-8.
A mustard-small measure of good is seen, the explicit fine grain of the section's exact moral separation.
A mustard-small measure of evil is likewise seen, completing 99:7's two-sided and exhaustive sorting.
When the graves are scattered in 82:4, each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind; bodily unearthing immediately yields the moral total.
The earth casts out what is inside it and becomes empty, staging extraction of buried contents rather than a merely verbal disclosure.
The certainty of the Hour includes God's raising everyone in the graves, the first extraction in the section's two-stage exposure.
At the trumpet blast people rush from the graves to their Lord, directly staging bodies leaving their buried containers.
People emerge from the graves like scattered locusts, making the buried multitude visible and separated across the scene.
People come rapidly out of the graves as though racing to a marker, another direct enactment of the section's first uncovering.
The earth splits open from around people as they hurry out, a forceful extraction from the enclosing ground.
At one call from God, people come out of the earth, condensing buried containment and sudden extraction into one act.
God causes the human being to die and be placed in a grave, establishing the bodily enclosure whose later opening the section parallels with the breast.
Then, when God wills, He raises that buried human, completing 80:21's enclosure-and-extraction sequence.
On the day people emerge fully exposed, nothing about them is hidden from God; bodily appearance and total divine disclosure coincide.
Each person's record is fastened to them and brought out on Resurrection as an open book, giving the accumulated deed-total an exposed form.
The person reads that opened record and is sufficient as their own reckoner, completing the final-account image of 17:13.
The human is informed that day of what was sent ahead and left behind, a final summation that loses no remainder.
The human self is a witness against itself, so the decisive account comes from within rather than from cultivated appearance.
Even offered excuses cannot cover the self-witness of 75:14, defining the limit of an outward shell once the interior testifies.
God raises everyone and informs them of their deeds: He has counted them although they forgot them, an exact picture of a complete accumulated total.
Everything people did is preserved in the records, supplying the gathered material for the final reckoning.
Every small and great thing is inscribed, specifying the exhaustive resolution of the record in 54:52.
Not an atom's weight, nor anything smaller or greater, escapes the Lord; all is in a clear record, matching the finest possible sorting.
The denied Hour will come, and no atom's weight in heaven or earth, smaller or greater, escapes the Knower of the unseen or its clear record.
God does not wrong even an atom's weight and multiplies good, grounding the section's minute distinction in exact justice.
وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون commands the guilty to separate themselves that day, turning judgment into an explicit sorting action.
God's book speaks with truth because every deed was transcribed, making the gathered record itself disclose the exact account.
A book speaks truth and no soul is burdened beyond capacity, presenting the record as an exact, non-distorting disclosure.
God has comprehended and counted every person exactly, a final enumeration corresponding to the source's completed total.
Each counted person comes to God alone on Resurrection, showing the individually isolated result of 19:94's enumeration.
Tongues, hands, and feet testify to what people did, forcing stored deeds into outward evidence.
Mouths are sealed while hands speak and feet testify to earnings, so the body's deeper record overrides its controlled exterior speech.
Hearing, sight, and skins testify against their owners, turning embodied experience into disclosed evidence.
The owners ask their skins why they testified, and the skins name God as the one who made everything speak, clarifying the involuntary disclosure of 41:20.
After deeds are seen, people return to the Knower of unseen and seen, who tells them what they were doing; action, hidden knowledge, and final report converge.
Showy charity is like thin soil stripped from smooth rock by rain, leaving nothing gained; removal of the cover reveals the deed's lack of inner substance.
Their bodies and speech impress outwardly, but they are likened to propped timbers; the striking manzar contains a contrary makhbar.
A person's worldly speech pleases and he invokes God over what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest opponent; polished exterior and inner reality diverge.
When that person turns away, he destroys crops and offspring; the action supplies the exposed fruit of the hidden antagonism in 2:204.
The Bedouins say they believe, but faith has not entered their hearts; the claimed outer identity is separated from the interior fact.
The ayah says eyes are not blind but the hearts within breasts are, making the visible organ and the inward faculty carry opposite verdicts.
The living and dead are not equal, and the unresponsive are pictured as those in graves; this metaphor reverses the source's image of worldly inner states as buried.
Failure belongs to the one who buries or corrupts the soul, the inverse of 91:9's purification and of the section's eventual extraction of what was inwardly buried.
The bad and good are not equal even when the bad's abundance impresses, a direct boundary between apparent quantity and sorted quality.
What people possess runs out while what is with God remains, stating the section's distinction between what passes away and the stable remainder.
Wealth and children are worldly adornment, while enduring righteous deeds are better with God, opposing loved goods to what survives the final accounting.
People prefer the nearer life, identifying the preference that sits inside the breast before it is exposed.
The Hereafter is better and more enduring, supplying the lasting side of the choice named in 87:16.
Some love rivals as they should love God, whereas believers are stronger in love for God; intensity of love is sorted by its object.
Love of desires, including heaped gold and silver, is beautified, but these are only the enjoyment of the nearer life.
After 3:14's decorated desires, the question “shall I tell you of better than that?” sets lasting reward against the beloved worldly shell.
Those who love worldly life over the Hereafter disclose a preference whose two objects will not have the same permanence.
People love the immediate life, naming the inner attachment on one side of the final disclosure.
They leave the Hereafter aside, completing the opposed preference stated by 75:20.
People love the immediate and leave behind a heavy day, directly opposing present attachment to the coming day of account.
The wealth-gatherer supposes wealth will make him last forever, a false claim of permanence overturned by the section's true final remainder.
The one whose scales are heavy enters the favorable side of the final separation.
A contented life is the outcome of the heavy scales in 101:6, stating what that measured remainder yields.
The one whose scales are light occupies the opposite side of the same exact weighing.
The abyss is the outcome of the light scales in 101:8, completing the judgment's two-way separation.
The true weighing that day makes those with heavy scales successful, treating the final account as measured substance.
Light scales identify those who lost themselves, completing 7:8's boundary at the weighing.
Heavy scales mark the successful in the final accounting.
Light scales mark those who lost themselves and remain in Hell, supplying the opposed result of 23:102.
A person's wealth does not avail when he falls, stripping accumulated goods of the permanence their lover assigns them.
The Prophet conceals within himself what God will disclose; although the context is a particular marriage, the same concealed-to-manifest relation is explicit.
Secret charity to the poor is better than displaying it, expiates wrongs, and ends with God as خبير of deeds, distinguishing visibility from moral value.
God does not take people to account for unintentional oath-speech but does for what their hearts have earned, locating accountable substance inwardly.
Hearing, sight, and heart will all be questioned, bringing the inward faculty itself into the reckoning.
People must not declare themselves pure, because God knows best who is mindful; self-presentation cannot substitute for known inner quality.
The oath by the soul and the One who fashioned it establishes the inner object purified or buried in 91:9-10.
Prosperity belongs to one who purifies himself, a compact parallel to inner refining before the following choice between present and enduring life.
God revives dead earth and brings grain out of it for people to eat, joining buried grain, extraction, and revival without explicitly depicting judgment.
Blessed rain produces gardens and harvest grain, giving the literal kernel and harvest side of the source's threshing image.
After the grain and provision of 50:9-10, revival of dead land is expressly compared to emergence, joining harvest to resurrection.
God splits the earth open, beginning the emergence of food from its enclosing ground.
Grain is then grown in the split earth, completing 80:26's opening-and-kernel scene.
A single حبة grows seven ears with a hundred grains each as a figure for expenditure, making a deed's hidden seed disclose its multiplied yield.
A crop ripens, yellows, and becomes broken debris, showing the visible plant reduced to its final residue as a reminder.
Worldly life is a crop that impresses, then yellows and becomes debris, concretely staging transient outer flourishing and its remainder.
Worldly vegetation becomes dry fragments scattered by winds, supplying the chaff-like passing side of the section's harvest image.
The deeds of disbelievers are ashes violently scattered by wind, a final account in which no useful remainder can be grasped.
God turns to the deeds people performed and makes them scattered dust, depicting an apparent store of action that yields no enduring substance.
The unbeliever's deeds are a mirage found empty, but he finds God there to pay his account fully; appearance is stripped and the true reckoning remains.
Enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and outcome, restating the stable remainder after temporary things recede.
Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is better and more lasting.
Worldly provision is temporary enjoyment, whereas what is with God is better and more enduring for believers.
Family, accumulated wealth, trade, and homes are tested as possible objects loved more than God and His cause, specifying what an inner attachment may contain.
The rivalry that reached the graves culminates in questioning about blessings, giving the accumulated life of 102:1-2 its account.
The slanderer gathers wealth and repeatedly counts it, a worldly counterfeit of the final divine gathering and total.
At judgment the person wishes he had sent something ahead for his true life, recognizing too late which part of worldly action would remain.
The destroyed army becomes like eaten crop-straw, supplying the discarded vegetal residue of the threshing image, though no moral winnowing is stated there.
The human doubts that God will gather his bones, posing the bodily gathering that precedes inner accounting.
God can restore even the fingertips, making the bodily gathering in 75:3 exact down to fine detail.
A single blast initiates the sudden transition from burial to exposure.
After the blast, people are upon the open surface, completing 79:13's compressed emergence scene.
After the cosmic coverings are removed, each soul knows what it has brought, giving disclosure its personal moral result.
God records what people send ahead and the traces they leave and enumerates everything in a clear register.
Everything has been enumerated in a book, a compact formulation of the completed account the source associates with tahsil.
Guardians remain over people, introducing the collection of deeds later known when graves are overturned.
The guardians are noble recorders, specifying how the accumulated account of 82:10 is preserved.
Those recorders know what people do, completing the record that 82:5 says each soul will finally know.
A human has only what he strives for, defining the substance that can remain in the personal account.
That striving will be seen, moving the inwardly accumulated effort into outward disclosure.
The striving is then repaid with the fullest recompense, completing the displayed account of 53:40.
God removes whatever rancor is in their breasts before Paradise, directly staging extraction of a stored inner content from the same vessel as 100:10.
God removes the rancor in their breasts and seats them as brothers, another explicit removal of what had been lodged inwardly.
God's purpose is to purify the believers and efface the disbelievers; the same refining family developed beside 3:154 is stated as the purpose of trial.

Following the threat to bring out hidden grudges in 47:29, this ayah says the hypocrites can be known by their marks and tone while God knows their deeds, showing inner content becoming legible outwardly.
A person says “we believe” but collapses under human persecution, and the ayah asks whether God best knows what all breasts contain; profession and inner fact are tested together.
God makes known the believers and the hypocrites, stating the discrimination produced by the trial described in 29:10.
Those who disbelieve return to God, are informed of what they did, and face the One who knows the contents of breasts; return, report, and inner knowledge coincide.
At judgment the covering is removed and sight becomes sharp, turning final disclosure into a literal stripping away of a veil.
God created the human and knows what the self whispers, locating divine knowledge at a level more inward than spoken or displayed action.
God is present to every secret counsel and will inform its participants of it on Resurrection, so concealed exchanges become items in the final report.
Those who think their secret and private counsel goes unheard are answered that divine messengers are recording it, joining concealment to accumulation in a record.
A good word is a good tree whose root is firm, giving the section's inner kernel a stable substance rather than a passing surface.
The firmly rooted tree of 14:24 continually gives its fruit, making hidden rooted quality disclose itself as lasting yield.
A bad word is an uprooted tree with no stability, the contrary result to the source's definition of what remains and becomes fixed.
God makes believers firm with the firm word in worldly life and the Hereafter, extending 14:24's rooted stability into final judgment.
Charity is taken from people's wealth to cleanse and purify them, joining the loved possession to an act that refines its holder inwardly.
True righteousness includes giving wealth despite loving it, so inner attachment is disclosed and transformed through relinquishment.
Joseph instructs people to leave harvested grain in its ears except what they eat; preserving the kernel inside its cover is a concrete inverse of stripping the husk away.
God causes human beings to grow from the earth like vegetation, fusing the grain image with bodily origin.
God returns people to the earth and will bring them out again, completing 71:17's plant-like origin with burial and extraction.
Human beings are created from earth, returned to it, and brought out from it once more, placing enclosure and final extraction in one ayah.
God removes the rage of believers' hearts, a present-life instance of an inwardly held condition being taken away.
God knows what is in the believers' hearts, sends tranquility upon them, and rewards them, grounding an outward pledge in known inner content.
A wall with an inner side of mercy and outer side of punishment separates hypocrites from believers on the final day, giving judgment a literal partition.

The hypocrites admit they once stood with the believers but inwardly tempted themselves, waited, doubted, and followed false hopes; the separation of 57:13 exposes a long-accumulated interior history.
Receiving the record in the left hand exposes the condemned person's negative final account after the universal presentation of 69:18.
The condemned person says his wealth did not avail him, stripping the intensely loved possession of substance at the moment the record is opened.
Immediately after the denunciation of immense love of wealth, the earth is pounded repeatedly, joining a threshing-like reduction of the ground to judgment's arrival.
Some say that they believe while they are not believers, separating an outward declaration from its inward truth.
A disease is in those speakers' hearts and grows because of their lying, identifying the inner content hidden by 2:8's profession.
The hypocrites voice a formally true testimony, yet God testifies that they are liars, distinguishing the statement's surface from the speakers' real stance.
A breast opened to submission and light is opposed to hardened hearts, making the breast's inward capacity and condition decisive.
Guidance is pictured as an expanded breast and misguidance as a constricted one, using the same inner vessel with opposite capacities.
People may dislike what is good for them and love what is bad for them while God knows and they do not, separating love's intensity from the beloved object's true value.
Opponents appear united, but their hearts are divided, a concise reversal between collected outward form and separated inner reality.
When truth comes, falsehood vanishes because falsehood is bound to vanish, supplying another exact boundary between what remains and what passes away.
Believers are asked why they say what they do not do, isolating the gap between verbal exterior and actual substance.
Saying what one does not do is gravely hateful to God, giving the mismatch named in 61:2 its moral judgment.
People are not left merely to say that they believe without being tested, so a verbal shell must undergo examination.
Earlier peoples were tested so that the truthful and liars would become known, stating the discriminating result of 29:2's trial.
The Helpers prefer others even amid their own need, and success belongs to those protected from inner greed, showing beloved goods sorted by generosity.
The command to spend is paired with success for those protected from the greed of their own souls, locating the obstacle to giving inside.
Greedily consuming inheritance supplies the concrete action that culminates in the immense love of wealth named in 89:20.
Believers are warned against hearts hardening as a long period passes, specifically supporting the source's picture of an interior altered by what accumulates over years.
God revives the earth after its death, offering a visible reversal immediately after 57:16's warning about hardened hearts.
The question about God expanding the Prophet's breast uses the inner vessel as something opened and made capacious, a secondary spatial sense relevant to what it can contain.
God brings out pasture, beginning a vegetal scene whose final residue appears in the next ayah.
The pasture becomes dark stubble, showing flourishing growth reduced to what remains after its useful life passes.
The world's luxuriant vegetation is suddenly made like a harvested field that had not flourished yesterday, an indirect harvest image of outward abundance passing away.
People incredulously ask whether they will be returned to their former state, setting up the bodily emergence completed in 79:13-14.
Their reference to decayed bones specifies the buried bodily material whose restoration they deny.
Believers are likened to a crop that sends out shoots, strengthens, thickens, and stands upright, making the quality of the seed visible in developed fruit.
Wind, cloud, and revived dead earth become an analogy for resurrection, joining vegetal emergence with bodies brought out after death.
God brings the living from the dead, revives earth after death, and says people will likewise be brought out, linking extraction and resurrection.
On judgment day disbelievers wish the earth could be leveled over them, yet they cannot conceal any statement from God; burial and failed concealment meet.
Hypocrites stand for prayer lazily to be seen by people, so a visible religious act bears a contrary inner motive.
Woe is directed at worshippers, introducing a judgment in which the outer act alone does not establish inward worth.
Those worshippers are heedless of their prayer, supplying the hidden defect beneath the act named in 107:4.
They perform for display, making the defective interior of 107:5 visible as a concern for outward appearance.
People love to be praised for what they did not do, linking inner love to an outward reputation detached from actual deeds.
